text:
maria: :rotating_light: Customer acme-app reporting 403s + unexpected billing spike after we rotated their API key this morning in eu-west-1. They say some requests succeeded and some got 403, and invoices show hits attributed to both old and new keys.

sam: can you paste the logs / repro steps? are they hitting via CDN or direct?

maria: they're behind our partner CDN. quick repro from their support ticket:
```
curl -i 'https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate?api_key=OLDKEY123' -H 'Host: eu.api.redwood.example.com'
```
some responses returned 200 (old key) and later 403s for the same path. header traces show x-forwarded-for from edge cache.

henry: sounds like the CDN cached a signed URL with the api_key query param. if we rotated and didn't purge, cached objects could continue using old key at the edge until TTL expires. but why both keys billed?

maria: hypothesis: CDN edge forwarded cached requests to an older routing tier which maps to our legacy billing shard that still recognizes OLDKEY123, while origin now enforces new key and returns 403 for direct requests. so some traffic takes the cached path (billed against old key) and some goes to origin (billed against new key but 403). customer sees double attribution.

janet: if that's true mitigation is: 1) purge CDN cache for that customer path 2) rotate/disable old key in billing system (or set old key to 401 immediately) 3) ask customer to stop using query-param auth and use header auth. we should also fix signed-URL generation to strip api_key from cacheable URLs.

mike: check Vault/KMS logs — was the old key revoked or just rotated? if old credential still unrevoked at storage layer, edges referencing it may still be valid for routing. also confirm KMS alias rewrap completed.

ops-bot: Alert: key-rotation-eu-west-1 completed by infra-runner at 1719876000. Vault rewrap succeeded, but cache-invalidation job failed (exit code 1).

maria: attaching relevant snippets from their trace (redacted):
```
Request: GET /v1/generate?api_key=OLDKEY123  -> 200 (edge cache hit)
Origin call: GET /v1/generate  X-API-Key: OLDKEY123 -> 403 (origin: key revoked)
Billing attribution: shard-legacy -> OLDKEY123: 12k tokens, shard-new -> NEWKEY456: 8k tokens
```

sam: ok. immediate actions: (A) purge CDN paths for acme-app (B) disable OLDKEY123 in auth service (C) inform billing to reverse/adjust legacy shard attribution pending reconciliation (D) create a short-term rule to reject any api_key query param at edge and respond 403 so cached URLs stop serving. can infra run those?

henry: I'm running the purge now and placing an edge rule to block query-param auth for that tag. also disabling OLDKEY123 in auth service. will follow up with logs.

billing-bot: Billing ticket created #BILL-1028 linking thread 1719876543, flagged for manual reconciliation.

janet: long-term: update our CDN signed-URL library to never include api keys in query strings; update docs + SDKs to prefer X-API-Key header; and ensure rotation playbook triggers CDN purge as a required step. logging an RFC for that.

maria: customer notified of mitigation steps and we offered to reconcile charges. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
